title: Repair and Emergency Service Calls: Counting Late-Payment Periods by Amount Paid
content:
On a late Repair and Emergency Service Calls invoice, the way charging periods of 30 days past the late-payment grace are counted depends on what the customer has paid toward the call. The records read are the call's payment lines and its charge lines (every charge on the invoice, late-payment charges included).

**Rule.** Which count applies depends on the share of the call's charges covered by the payments posted on the call.

| Payments posted on the call | How the charging periods past the grace are counted |
|---|---|
| At least a quarter (25 percent) of its charges | Only charging periods that have run in full are counted |
| Something, but less than a quarter of its charges | The periods run in full are counted, and a period still running counts as half a period (0.5) |
| Nothing | Every period started counts in full, the first one from the first day past the grace |

The same count is used both for the periods counted now and for the periods counted as of the posting date of the call's latest late-payment charge line.

## Periods counted by days past the grace

| Days past the grace | At least a quarter paid | Less than a quarter paid | Nothing paid |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 0.5 | 1 |
| 30 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 31 | 1 | 1.5 | 2 |
| 45 | 1 | 1.5 | 2 |
| 60 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| 61 | 2 | 2.5 | 3 |

## The quarter boundary (hypothetical invoice with $400.00 of charges)

- Payments of $100.00 are exactly a quarter, so only full periods count.
- Payments of $99.99 are less than a quarter, so full periods count and a running period counts as half.
- No payment means every started period counts in full.
